searchTerms.key: everything you're scared to lose was never yours

tests.question: Does the second Short reach more people in the morning than in the afternoon?
tests.why: Across 294 Shorts, each against its own week: 00-03 UTC 1.15x, 04-11 UTC 1.0x, 12-19 UTC 0.75x. Since October 19 the afternoon Short got a median 0.63x of the same day's evening Short, and six of them stalled under 90 views.
tests.measure: The second Short's day-1 views divided by the same day's first Short's, for 14 days, against the median before.
tests.approved: 2026-11-06: owner, in the HQ: "Yes, move it"

tests.question: Do a real description and a question under each Short get viewers talking?
tests.change: Every edit's description opens with three short paragraphs about the viewer's own life and asks one question ("💬 Question: ... Share your thoughts in the comments."), modelled on the viral Short the owner sent; the same question is the channel's comment under the Short, instead of "Which line hit hardest? Write it below." On every Short from November 6: the owner wants it on all of them, so it is not an A/B.
tests.why: Through November 5, viewers left 5 comments on 51 edits (0.48 per 1,000 views). Comments are one of the signals YouTube ranks on, and a question about the viewer's own life is easier to answer than one about the video.
tests.measure: Comments from viewers per 1,000 views on the Shorts in the new style (14 days from the start) against the Shorts of the 14 days before; likes per 100 views alongside.
tests.approved: 2026-11-06: owner, in the HQ, on this test's card: a viral Short's description, "use it as inspiration for pur next shorts"

tests.question: Do playlists per philosopher bring in extra views?
tests.change: Three public playlists ("Marcus Aurelius quotes: Stoic Shorts", the same for Seneca and Epictetus), with every public edit filed under its philosopher, newest first, and each new Short added the day it airs. A Short the prune bot unlists is taken out, so the playlists show the ones still on the channel.
tests.why: Someone who liked one Short can watch that philosopher's others in a row, and the playlists can show up when people search for him.
tests.measure: The share of the channel's views that come from playlists (YouTube's traffic sources), the 14 days after against the 14 before.
tests.approved: 2026-11-06: owner, in the HQ: "Yes, make the playlists"

tests.question: Do the searches people make bring more of them to our Shorts?
tests.change: Each Short's description opens with the YouTube search its quote answers ("How to stop overthinking: Epictetus's answer."), a matching hashtag joins #stoicism, and the search goes into the tags. Ten searches, picked from YouTube's own suggestions (data/search_phrases.json, data/search_research.md). The title carries it too only if the owner picks titles.
tests.why: Since June, YouTube search brought 225 views, all from broad words (stoicism, marcus aurelius). Searches like "how to stop overthinking" are among YouTube's most popular, and brought us none: our Shorts never use those words.
tests.measure: The share of views from YouTube search, the 14 days after against the 14 before.
tests.approved: 2026-11-07: owner, in the HQ: "Yes: descriptions, hashtags and tags" (titles stay as they are)

tests.question: Does the crew's new look (painted shots, a hook readable on the first frame, YouTube-level sound) bring more views?
tests.change: Every Short from 2026-11-12: each shot a colour painting from the free FLUX.2 model (inspected before it airs), the v2 type with gold key words, sound mastered to -14 LUFS.
tests.why: This month's top Stoicism Shorts are painted, colourful and readable on frame one; ours were washed-out black-and-white stock with a grey first frame and quieter sound.
tests.measure: The median edit's views at 3 days old, the 14 days after against the 14 before.
tests.approved: 2026-11-11: owner, in the HQ: "Switch to the new look"

tests.question: Does a follow line at the end of every description turn more viewers into subscribers?
tests.change: The last line of every edit's description, before the hashtags: "One Stoic line a day. Follow for tomorrow's."
tests.why: 98% of views come from people who don't follow the channel (Glaux, 28 days to 11-06); it gains about 1.5 subscribers a day and 1,000 by the end of 2027 needs 1.8. The cheapest ask there is.
tests.measure: New subscribers per 1,000 views, the 14 days after against the 14 before (channel_stats.csv).
tests.approved: 2026-11-12: within the autonomy rule (words only, reversible); on the owner's Ideas board as idea-follow-line

tests.question: Does a third Short a day, in the evening window, add views a day without starving each Short?
tests.change: From 2026-11-13: three posts a day (MAX_POSTS_PER_DAY 3); the third waits for 19:00 UTC (POST_SLOT_HOURS 0,7,19; the 19:00 and 23:00 crons post it), at least 5 hours apart.
tests.why: The 2027 goal needs about 2,740 views a day; two Shorts make about 1,200. Each Short reaches 600 to 950 people in its first days whatever the slot, and the evening slot got 1.15x the reach of its week, so a third post should add roughly 40%.
tests.measure: Views a day (Cicero's funnel, the 14 days after against the 14 before) and the median Short's views at 3 days old, so a third post that only splits the same views shows up.
tests.approved: 2026-11-13: owner, in the HQ: "A third Short a day, in the evening: Go"
